:::{#exm-indpt-pmf-fails}
#### The PMF form fails for continuous random variables

The factorization in @thm-indpt-pmf does not work as a definition of independence
for continuous random variables:
there, both sides are $0$ at every point,
so it would call every pair of continuous random variables independent.
For instance,
let $X \sim \text{Uniform}(0, 1)$ ([uniform distribution](random-variables.qmd#def-uniform)),
whose density is $1$ on $[0, 1]$,
and let $Y = X$.
For all real numbers $x$ and $y$,
the event $\set{X = x,\, Y = y}$ is $\set{X = x}$ if $y = x$ and empty otherwise,
so it has probability $0$,
because $\Pr(X = x) = 0$ for the [continuous](random-variables.qmd#def-continuous-rv) $X$.
Likewise

$$
\begin{aligned}
\Pr(X = x)\,\Pr(Y = y) &= 0 \cd 0 \\
&= 0,
\end{aligned}
$$

so the PMF form holds.
But $X$ and $Y$ are not independent:

$$
\ba
\Pr(X \in [0, \tfrac{1}{2}],\, Y \in [0, \tfrac{1}{2}])
&= \Pr(X \in [0, \tfrac{1}{2}])
&& \text{(} Y = X \text{)} \\
&= \int_0^{1/2} 1\,dx
&& \text{(the density of } X \text{ is } 1 \text{ on } [0, 1] \text{)} \\
&= \tfrac{1}{2}
&& \text{(integrate)}
\ea
$$

while

$$
\begin{aligned}
\Pr(X \in [0, \tfrac{1}{2}])\,\Pr(Y \in [0, \tfrac{1}{2}]) &= \tfrac{1}{2} \cd \tfrac{1}{2} \\
&= \tfrac{1}{4}.
\end{aligned}
$$

:::
